See also: Bandera, bandêra, bandéra, banderą, and Banderą

Aragonese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Spanish bandera.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /banˈdeɾa/
  • Syllabification: ban‧de‧ra
  • Rhymes: -eɾa

Noun

[edit]

bandera f (plural banderas)

  1. flag

References

[edit]
  • Diccionario ortografico de l'aragonés (Seguntes la PO de l'EFA)
  • Bal Palazios, Santiago (2002), “bandera”, in Dizionario breu de a luenga aragonesa, Zaragoza, →ISBN

bandera f (plural banderes)

bandera

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [bənˈde.ɾə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [banˈde.ɾa]
  • Audio (Catalonia):(file)

Noun

[edit]

bandera f (plural banderes)

  1. flag

  • bandera espanyola

  • banderó

Cebuano

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Spanish bandera, from banda +‎ -era.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Hyphenation: ban‧de‧ra

Noun

[edit]

bandera

  1. a flag
  2. a banner
  3. a type of kite that is shaped like a flag

Makasar

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Portuguese bandeira.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /banˈdera/, [ɓãn.ˈde.ra]
  • Hyphenation: ban‧de‧ra

Noun

[edit]

bandera (Lontara spelling ᨅᨉᨙᨑ)

  1. flag
  2. (card games) one of the thirty types of cards in the patui and goang-gòng game

Derived terms

[edit]
affixations
  • aʼbandera
  • paʼbanderàng
compounds
  • lambaru bandera
  • tukang bandera

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Dhuwal: bandirra'
  • → Iwaidja: bandirran
  • → Maung: pantirrang
  • → Tiwi: pantirra

Further reading

[edit]
  • A. A. Cense (2024), Makassaars-Nederlands woordenboek‎[1], Brill, →DOI

Polish

[edit]
Polish Wikipedia has an article on:
bandera
Wikipedia pl

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish, from Italian bandiera.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /banˈdɛ.ra/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛra
  • Syllabification: ban‧de‧ra
  • Homophone: Bandera

Noun

[edit]

bandera f

  1. ensign (the principal flag or banner flown by a ship to indicate nationality)

[edit]
Declension of bandera
singular plural
nominative bandera bandery

dative banderze banderom
accusative banderę bandery
instrumental banderą banderami
locative banderze banderach
vocative bandero bandery

Derived terms

[edit]
adjective
  • banderowy
noun
  • tania bandera

  • bandera in Polish dictionaries at PWN

Serbo-Croatian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • bandijera (dialectal)

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian bandiera (“flag, flag pole”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /banděːra/
  • Hyphenation: ban‧de‧ra

Noun

[edit]

bandéra f (Cyrillic spelling банде́ра)

  1. pole (as in telephone pole or electric pole)
  2. (Chakavian) flag
  3. (Chakavian) flag pole

Declension

[edit]
Declension of bandera
singular plural
nominative bandera bandere
genitive bandere bandera
dative banderi banderama
accusative banderu bandere
vocative bandero bandere
locative banderi banderama
instrumental banderom banderama

Synonyms

[edit]
  • (flag): zȃstava

  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -eɾa
  • Syllabification: ban‧de‧ra

Noun

[edit]

bandera f (plural banderas)

  1. flag
  2. banner

Tagalog

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish bandera. Compare Malay bendera. Doublet of bandila, an earlier borrowing.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /banˈdeɾa/ [bɐn̪ˈd̪ɛː.ɾɐ]
  • Rhymes: -eɾa
  • Syllabification: ban‧de‧ra

Noun

[edit]

bandera (Baybayin spelling ᜊᜈ᜔ᜇᜒᜇ)

  1. flag; banner; standard
    Synonyms: watawat, bandila
  2. (colloquial) act of showing off or parading something

Derived terms

[edit]
  • banderahan
  • ibandera
  • magbandera

Related terms

[edit]
  • abanderado
  • banda
  • bandereta
  • banderilya
  • banderin

Further reading

[edit]
  • “bandera”, in Pambansang Diksiyonaryo | Diksiyonaryo.ph, 2018

Anagrams

[edit]
  • beranda
